client_brief:
DAYDRIFT: Three vertical short cuts with cleaned speech

Project overview
DAYDRIFT is a slow, unhurried interview show built around one guest and one real conversation that runs the better part of an hour. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Three vertical short cuts with cleaned speech and DAYDRIFT season four episode stills.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (3 measured short files); motion_source_metadata.json; source_video_files/ (3 measured short files); daydrift_mic_flag.jpg; daydrift_card_2025.pdf; daydrift_season4.csv; daydrift_shownotes.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Three vertical short cuts with cleaned speech: A deliberate 10-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 3 supplied short clips using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. 
- DAYDRIFT season four episode stills: Three representative pictures, one pulled from each of the three episodes, brought to one channel target with one white point, one black point, one warmth and one sense of room, each at or below its own recording's dimensions, with a per picture parameter...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 3 video files totaling 15.126 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 0 separate audio files. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com YouTube podcast post carried in the ledger, where a two person show hands over raw episode recordings and asks for episodes shaped into something watchable, for light hearted graphics that match a casual fun vibe, for the client's existing logo carried across the channel branding, and for any custom graphic assets created to be delivered separately in transparent PNG or vector form. Two literal asks in that post are not connector work and are re cast honestly rather than faked. A timeline trim of pauses and stumbles has no connector analogue, because the shortening tool works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the short vertical pieces are produced by that route and the brief asks for short cuts rather than for a re edited episode. Motion graphics composited over the picture are also unavailable, so the caption plate and the end card are delivered as editable canvases the show drops into its own editor, and the brief asks for a plate rather than for burned in captions. Everything else in that post is now genuinely producible: CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms an ink level recovery off photographed printed collateral, a merge template reverse engineered out of a flat press PDF, and a native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes, which is exactly the separately delivered, client editable asset set the poster asked for and never got.

price_band_and_audience: Independent long form podcast, eight dollar monthly membership, one modest renewing sponsor, listeners thirty to fifty. The band is load bearing. At this level the look has to read considered and hand made: warm domestic light, real texture in the room, restrained type, the picture of two people talking rather than a set. Push it toward broadcast, with a hard lit black seamless, a hard geometric grid and a network style lockup, and it misrepresents a two person show to the exact membership that pays for it because it is not that. Push it the other way into a scrappy meme treatment, with heavy outlines, arrows and shouted type, and it reads as the wrong genre entirely for a fifty minute interview and the sponsor renewal argument collapses. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent long form interview podcast with a YouTube channel, one guest per episode, made and recorded in the show's own room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A two person show: two hosts, one room, nine episodes a season.
brand_identity.about: DAYDRIFT is a slow, unhurried interview show built around one guest and one real conversation that runs the better part of an hour. It is made by two people in a room they know well, funded by a small paying membership and one renewing sponsor. The promise is intimacy: you are sitting in on a talk between people who like each other, not watching a broadcast.
brand_identity.audience: Regular listeners aged thirty to fifty, most of them listening at work through the day. About two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, plus a few thousand free listeners who click through to the channel page.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Membership at eight dollars a month with one modest renewing sponsor. Squarely independent: above hobby, well below a network production. The look must read considered and hand made, never broadcast and never scrappy meme.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist serif for the show name and episode titles, paired with a quiet humanist sans for credits, dates and body. Generous spacing, restrained weights, nothing condensed or shouted. Type should feel like a good paperback, not a title card.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and a little understated, the way two friends actually talk. We never oversell a guest. Example line the brand would write: "Episode eight. We sat down with her for an hour and did not want it to end."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files left. The show name only survives as artwork on the foam flag on the microphone, drawn years ago by a friend who has since moved away and left no source file. Last season's printed episode card exists only as the print file the printer returned. Everything else has to be rebuilt from those.
brand_identity.values: Honesty and warmth over polish. The show would rather be small and real than slick, and it wants a look it can keep running itself next season without re commissioning.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_mic_flag.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the show's foam microphone flag standing on the desk, the wordmark printed in one deep ink across the soft foam face.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our name still exists as artwork."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The wordmark is disjoint lettering on a soft compressible surface, so the one call knockout keeps two or three letters, drops the rest and still returns success. The ink has spread into the foam, so the strokes are heavier and the counters tighter than the drawing ever was, which is invisible at full canvas and decisive at reproduction size. The flag's own colour also runs close to the wall behind it down the shadowed side of the frame.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's episode card exactly as it went to the printer: single sided A6, episode number, title, guest credit, recording date, sponsor line and one picture window.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer made for us last year. We still have the print file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What that card becomes when it is opened as an editable document is nothing like what the printed page suggests. Its face can collapse into one continuous text frame carrying every line, with no separately addressable picture frame at all. The readout that lists that frame's text also drops one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short, and both the validator and the template preparation report success on the wrong offsets.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_season4.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The season roster: nine episodes with number, title, guest, recording date, runtime, sponsor line and a per record picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every episode this season, exactly as we list them on the site."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One guest appears twice under two different spellings, and one episode title runs long enough that a fixed measure stops rendering it rather than pushing it, so the record reads complete in the data and arrives cut short at trim. The picture column also names nine pictures when only three episodes have been asked for as frames, which no column heading admits.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_shownotes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the nine episode titles, the one line guest credits, the recording dates and the sponsor read line that is contractually required to appear on the card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Titles and credits as we publish them. The sponsor line is not ours to shorten."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the silent final piece still communicates clearly without implying dialogue, ambience, or music that was never supplied.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Strengthen visual sequencing or approved on-screen copy without fabricating a soundtrack.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The deliverable relies on absent sound and fails when viewed as supplied.
